actual_scope: Characteristic polynomial, over Q, of the eigenvalue-+1 eigenspace of s=(0 4 3 7)(5 6) on the moved c=1 sign character eps[1]*eps[2]. The other three real 48-dimensional eigenspaces of this s are compared and are not the 216-dimensional joint eigenspace.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a formal caller or certificate binding. PR #7009 leaves the characteristic polynomial of one 48-dimensional eigenspace of s on a moved 192-character uncomputed. This package answers that polynomial for the real eigenvalue +1 on the character eps[1]*eps[2]. It does not add a Lean binding.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The selected conditional kappa remains 781451/250000000. The one-slot minimal polynomial remains degree 881 in research/exact-one-slot-gram/; this polynomial locates one invariant subspace inside that certificate and does not replace it.
stop_rule: Stop once one explicit 48-dimensional basis and the characteristic polynomial of A_1 on it are recomputed from the pinned query, with the matrix pinned and the factorisation checked. Do not rerun the degree-881 certificate, do not build an eigenvalue-i basis, and do not search the centralizer.
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the basis and the 48-by-48 integer matrix of B=4 A_1. Marker PASS_C1_MOVED_48_CHARPOLY. chi_A SHA256 1230f7227b6cbd0ad1383273a601bb4f517462ca663235c673e6b6bb13f1b3af. Eigenvalue -1 on the same character is isospectral. The character eps[5]*eps[6] has a different polynomial. Selected baseline returned PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY.

open_questions.question: What is the characteristic polynomial, over Q(i), of one eigenvalue-i eigenspace of s on the character eps[1]*eps[2]?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The same element s has four complex eigenvalues of multiplicity 48 on this character. Only the real eigenvalues +1 and -1 are computed here, so half of the moved 192-character is still not located inside the degree-881 polynomial.
open_questions.first_step: Solve s v = i v together with the character equations over Z[i], using the same least-index orbit basis, and repeat the Hessenberg Chinese-remainder computation in that ring.
open_questions.blocked_by: The integer orbit basis in this package solves eigenvalue equations in {+1,-1} and does not list a Q(i) basis.

open_questions.question: What is the geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 for A_1 on this pinned 48-dimensional space?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The characteristic polynomial gives algebraic multiplicity 10 and is not square-free, so it is not the minimal polynomial. The rational nullity of the pinned matrix is the geometric multiplicity. This is not the 216-by-216 matrix of the joint eigenspace of g and t.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the exact rank over Q of the pinned 48-by-48 integer matrix of B.
open_questions.blocked_by: A modular rank is only a lower bound on the rational rank, and this package does not run the exact elimination.
